# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1–36 (Updated 2026-10-13, Final)

## Setting and Time
- **Current Period**: Winter of ninth year after Waterloo (1830). Story spans from Sunday, 26th April dinner (Chapters 1–35) through Chapter 36 (winter). Dinner for Emperor of China scheduled Monday, 8th July (three weeks ahead as of Chapter 35). Chapter 36 set in market towns (Bryngate, Mirecombe, Coldcombe, Dunholt) and London (Welbeck Street).
- **Key Locations**: London (Welbeck Street, Grosvenor Square, Abchurch Lane, Beargarden Club, Langham Hotel, Euston Square Railway Station, Bruton Street, Lincoln's Inn, Queen's Gate, Islington, Pall Mall East, Trafalgar Square); Coventry Island; Queen's Crawley; rural areas (Sheep's Acre Farm, Coldcombe, Mirecombe, Gulton, Harrowgate, Beccles, Bryngate, Dunholt, Salwick); international (Ostend, Brussels, New York, San Francisco, Liverpool, Kansas, Oregon).

## Major Deaths
John Sedley, Mr. Osborne, Joseph Sedley, Colonel Rawdon Crawley, Sir Pitt, Wevie Lindner (died winter, buried Salmere).

## Rebecca's Arc
Never became Lady Crawley; styles herself so. Son (Sir Rawdon) receives allowance but refuses to see her. Appears wealthy at Bath/Cheltenham, busies herself with piety and Charity Lists.

## Amelia and William Dobbin
Married at Ostend; Amelia initiated encounter. Dobbin quit service, rented "the Evergreens" (Hampshire). Devoted father; daughter Jane his pride.

## Lady Carbury and Family

**Lady Carbury**: Welbeck Street resident with Felix and Henrietta. Authored "Criminal Queens." Crushed by "Evening Pulpit" review (Mr. Jones/Alf's reviewer); praised by "Morning Breakfast Table" (Mr. Broune). Counseled Felix to elope with Marie immediately. **Chapter 35: Took initiative; wrote note inviting Melmotte to drawing-room. Attempted introductions to Mr. Alf and Mr. Broune. Late Chapter 35 (after 2 A.M.): Mr. Broune proposed marriage. Found instead he had human heart she could touch. Asked him to leave. Promised written answer by Thursday. By six o'clock evening: Sent rejection letter via Didon to Pall Mall East. Full of regrets; thrown away firm footing. In debt; feared unpaid baker, son's horses, his dissipation. Lying had become her nature. Chapter 36: Attended soirée of learned people with Roger Carbury; returned home to find Paul and Henrietta together. Disbelieved Paul's claim visit was accidental, though Roger believed him. Angry at finding them alone. Cross-examined Henrietta on intentions regarding Paul. Expressed scorn at Henrietta's suggestion of marrying for railway fortune, despite her own efforts to secure advantageous matches for Felix. Allowed Henrietta to leave after kissing.**

**Felix Carbury**: Beautiful; cynosure of mother's eyes. Won £2,000 from Lord Grasslough, £400 from Miles Grendall at gaming. Director of South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway. Thursday evening at Grosvenor Square: Kissed Marie's lips when alone. Melmotte offered advancement if Felix withdraws from suit; offered £200 cheque. **Chapter 35: Returned home nearly drunk. Made appointment with Ruby Ruggles at kitchen-garden bottom (Sheep's Acre); neglected it without intending to. Heard nothing from London lover for three weeks. Later: Melmotte suggested Felix could make money in city if sure of it, loss of Marie would not break heart. Felix asked Melmotte: "could you let me have those shares?" Chapter 35 (late): Ashamed of himself; knew he was treating Ruby badly. Consoled himself by reflecting that writing renunciation letter would not prevent running away with her if worth his while. Chapter 36: Wrote letter to Ruby excusing himself, claiming summoned to Liverpool on American railway business. Had been corresponding with Mr. Ramsbottom at Liverpool. Ramsbottom suggested he visit; his conduct at Board resulted from Ramsbottom's advice, though dread of interview with Mrs. Hurtle may have added strength to invitation.**

**Henrietta Carbury**: Rejected Roger's suit (too young, age disparity). Within week, Paul returned "as still dear friend," promising not to see her three months. Wore rose from Roger's room. When meeting Roger at door, showed "more graciousness towards him than he had ever seen before." Roger declared love anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. Paul Montague thoroughly in love with her. **Chapter 36: Paul visited her at Welbeck Street in Lady Carbury's absence (claimed accident; Roger believed him though circumstances suspicious). When discovered together, Henrietta felt caught though innocent. Mother cross-examined her intentions. Hetta expressed admiration for Roger as "rock of strength" and praised his honesty; told Paul Roger "never lies. He never takes what is not his own." Declared to mother: "He is so much above me, that, though I do love him, I cannot think of him in that way. And I have told you that I do love some one else. I have no secret from you now." Kissed mother and left room after mother's anger softened.**

## Ruby Ruggles
Granddaughter of Daniel Ruggles (Sheep's Acre, Sheepstone, near Bungay). Pretty with long glossy ringlets, large dark eyes, clear complexion. Felix preferred Ruby to Marie. Made appointment at kitchen-garden; waited in vain. For three weeks heard nothing but constantly thought of him. **Chapter 35: After John Crumb arrived with Joe Mixet for supper, received them with cool indifference. While men smoked, fled to yard. After Mixet's departure, John made motion toward Ruby putting out right hand. Ruby escaped to bedside, afraid to undress. Subsequently took herself off from farm entirely.**

**John Crumb & Suitor Plans**: Country lover. **Chapter 35: After supper, moved to take Ruby's hand. Ruby fled. Rode to Carbury Hall searching for her. Grandfather (after consulting Roger and Father Barham) had horses being put to carriage for Beccles railway station when John arrived. Asked grandfather: "Ye ain't a' found her, Mr. Ruggles, ha' ye?" Chapter 36: Roger confirmed to Paul that John "certainly has known her. Though he lied, as he always lies, when I first spoke to him, I brought him to admit that he and she had been friends down in Suffolk." Roger noted John lies habitually about money and circumstances but will eventually become perfect liar with age.**

**Daniel Ruggles**: Holds Sheep's Acre Farm on bishop's lease; Roger Carbury's tenant. **Chapter 35: Consulted Roger and Father Barham at Carbury Hall about Ruby's departure. Revealed: Ruby "liked him [John] well enough till she'd seed somebody else." Made most of Ruby's bad behaviour. Roger and Father Barham ordered waggonette to Beccles railway station to search for her.**

## The Melmottes

**Augustus Melmotte**: Chairman, South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Company. Arrived London from Paris within two years; claims English birth but accent betrays "long expatriation." Big man with large whiskers; expression of mental power on harsh vulgar face. Rumours of gigantic swindler gaining ground. Candidate for Westminster parliament seat. Planning great dinner for Emperor of China (Monday, 8th July). **Chapter 35: Board meeting: Addressed directors regarding company prosperity; proposed adjournment one week without disclosing particulars. When Paul Montague pressed for details, responded curtly. Beckoned Felix privately. Suggested adding Sir Merton Longestaffe senior or Adolphus Longestaffe senior as director, offering either replacement for Montague if he resigned, or additional directorship if he stayed. Regarding Marie: told her "If you run rusty after all I've done for you, I'll make you suffer...He wants money, not you." Offered Felix terms: if Felix renounces suit in writing, Melmotte will "stick to you and make a man of you" and give £200 cheque. On word of honour as gentleman: if daughter married Felix, she'd never have single shilling; would immediately make will leaving all property to St. George's Hospital. Chapter 36: When Paul wanted to see him, bolted into inner room but took Felix with him, suggesting possible consent to marriage.**

**Marie Melmotte**: Speaks English well; forming own opinions. Rejected Lord Grasslough; experienced with Lord Nidderdale. Secretly instructed Felix to find father. Resolved on constancy toward Felix. Thursday evening: Felix kissed her lips. She said "Now be brave." Delivered note revealing papa settled money on her in France (undoable without her leave); she refused to give Felix up. **Chapter 35: Now engaged to Lord Nidderdale (not Felix). More than week since seeing Felix. Nidderdale spoke of stern governors; Marie said "It's an awful bore." Not wedded to Grosvenor Square grandeur; unafraid of starvation if married to Felix. As soon as Nidderdale left, wrote again to Felix begging to hear from him; entrusted letter to Didon. Father intends she marry Nidderdale, fixed August wedding date. Marie declared: "It is no use, father, for I will never have him."**

**Madame Melmotte**: **Chapter 35: Informing Miss Longestaffe she would not sit at Emperor dinner-table but received evening ticket for herself and joint ticket for gentleman and wife. Georgiana initially indignant but accepted.**

## The Longestaffes

**Sir Merton Longestaffe**: Determined no more London expenses; family will not return from Caversham. Desires to sell Pickering and disembarrass Caversham from debt. Dolly refused consent unless half produce given to him. Chapter 34: Received thunderbolt letter from Dolly that Melmottes must be "very bad indeed," angered by passage suggesting he should have taken family to town. Negotiating sale.

**Georgiana Longestaffe**: Made strong protest against Melmottes. Following morning received undated invitation to stay with them. By Sunday, present at Grosvenor Square. **Chapter 35: Wrote troublesome letter to old friend Lady Monogram (formerly Julia Triplex). Julia replied: husband Sir Damask forbids calling on Melmottes; they've "got into different sets." Julia refused to have Melmottes "crammed down their throats." Georgiana (unmarried twelve years) sobbed when Sir Damask entered. Sir Damask led her out, put her in Madame Melmotte's carriage.**

**Adolphus (Dolly) Longestaffe**: Has rooms in Bruton Street. Chapter 34: Called on sister early afternoon; she complained of confinement. Within half hour received lawyer's letter regarding Pickering sale. States father cannot sell without his consent. Asked for half the plunder (£25,000 would pay off what he owes). Expects father to give in. States Melmotte will advance him £1,000, allowing Felix to get railway shares. Agreed with Felix on plan to visit Abchurch Lane at 2 P.M. next day. Mid-week: Dined with Felix at Beargarden.

## South Central Pacific and Mexican Railway Scheme

**The Enterprise**: Railway from Salt Lake City, branching from San Francisco/Chicago line, through New Mexico/Arizona into Mexico, terminating Vera Cruz. Approximately 2,000 miles.

**Financial Strategy**: Stock at par; shares sold at premium "to run them up even to 110," yielding minimum three hundred thousand dollars. Directors understood fortune made by floating shares, not building railway.

**London Directorate**: Melmotte (chairman), Lord Alfred Grendall, Sir Felix Carbury, Samuel Cohenlupe (MP for Staines), Lord Nidderdale, Paul Montague.

## Paul Montague and Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle

**Paul's Situation**: Living at Beargarden. Junior railway firm member. Personally dislikes Fisker. Trembles for his money. Thoroughly in love with Hetta; not in love with Mrs. Hurtle. Only Hetta serves as confidant. **Chapter 35: Board meeting—pressed Melmotte for company details; challenged him on shares and scrip issued. Melmotte cut him short. Chapter 36: Returned from Liverpool Friday morning before Board meeting. Felt must tell Mrs. Hurtle face-to-face he would not marry her due to dissatisfaction with her past life. After Board, joined Nidderdale's table at Beargarden. Nidderdale questioned Paul regarding Melmotte's trustworthiness. Paul said "I don't see why it shouldn't be all true. Nobody, I take it, knows very much about him." When Nidderdale left, occurred to him he'd "be coming a cropper rather" were he to marry Marie for her money, then find she had none. Later visited Hetta at Welbeck Street; claimed visit accidental. Walked with Roger Carbury to Roger's hotel after evening together. Roger asked him about Ruby Ruggles matter and confirmed John Crumb's dishonesty.**

**Mrs. Winifrid Hurtle**: Formerly betrothed to Paul. Arrived Wednesday (after Liverpool Tuesday). During earlier engagement promised to follow him; saw him in New York on second San Francisco journey, renewed promises. Theatre evening: Paul took her; she addressed play's portrayal of woman whose lover talked to another, noting position described was nearly her own. After theatre, declined Paul's cab offer but he accompanied anyway. Remarked London's immensity and dirt; compared New York. Called Paris "gem of gems." Does not like Frenchmen; likes Englishmen better than Americans; fancies could never like English women. Hates "buckram" and forced propriety. Thinks: He should marry her or world should hear story of his perjury. Believes he promised marriage. **Chapter 36: Paul must decide line of conduct; she must know truth.**

## Lord Nidderdale
Intent on marrying Marie for fortune. Claims not afraid of Melmotte, believing he "rather likes me." **Chapter 35: Marie now engaged to Nidderdale. Chapter 36: At Beargarden with Paul. Questioned Paul regarding Melmotte's trustworthiness. Expressed concern about marrying for money if money doesn't exist. Later: "I suppose I shall,--if I don't die first. But I should have gone on with the horses just the same if there had never been anything to come;--only they wouldn't have given me tick, you know."**

## Mr. Broune
Editor, "Morning Breakfast Table" (managing morning paper—"heavier burden" than afternoon). Commercial articles deemed "gospel." Nearer fifty than sixty; young of his age. **Chapter 35 (late evening): Came to Lady Carbury's with perturbation. Determined to ask her to be his wife. When he read her rejection letter: stood at fireplace, left letter on table. Woman wasn't in love with him! She had shown love by thousand signs. Gradually felt admiration greater than ever.**

## Roger Carbury
Nearly forty. Never owed shilling he couldn't pay; father likewise. Firmly opposed Melmotte connection on principle. Took Oxford degree; became "pervert," supposed "convert." Works as priest on day-labourer's wages; forced to buy second-hand clothes. Soft heart; knows Lady Carbury false and Felix worthless. Declared love to Henrietta anew (Chapter 32 evening); determination unshaken. **Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall; consulted by Daniel Ruggles and Father Barham about Ruby. Ordered waggonette to Beccles. Chapter 36: Attended soirée of learned people in London; returned to Welbeck Street with Lady Carbury, found Paul and Henrietta together. Suspected circumstances though believed Paul's accidental visit explanation. Walked with Paul afterward to his hotel. Confided that Ruby Ruggles disappeared from neighbourhood; confirmed John Crumb knew her as "friends" in Suffolk and lied about it. Noted Crumb habitually lies about money but will eventually become perfect liar with maturity.**

## Other Characters
- **Miles Grendall**: Secretary to Melmotte. Does not pay debts of honour.
- **Lord Grasslough**: Remarked rumors suggesting Melmotte "robber" but "wonderful fellow."
- **Marquis of Auld Reekie**: Nidderdale's father. Fierce-looking, gouty, watery eyes, stiff grey-white hair.
- **Father John Barham**: Priest, Beccles. Dogmatic Catholic. **Chapter 35: At Carbury Hall with Daniel Ruggles and Roger.**
- **Joe Mixet**: John Crumb's friend. **Chapter 35: Came to Sheep's Acre supper.**
- **Madame Didon**: Carries messages between Marie and Felix.
- **Mr. Ramsbottom**: Liverpool gentleman. Suggested Paul visit; his advice resulted in Paul's Board conduct. Chapter 36: Paul corresponded with him regarding Mrs. Hurtle matter. Offered Felix business opportunity.
- **Rural Characters (Chapter 36)**: Bryngate/Mirecombe/Coldcombe/Dunholt locations feature: cart with turnips, frost-silvered hedges, vesper bells, threatening rain, oven queues, crooked sun chalked on forge wall, various unnamed townsfolk including Rozek, Aewyn Brackwood, Seena Hollett, Conar Hollett, Lubin Brackwood, Isnar Brackwood, Hamira Hollwood, Thivie, Dalde Brackwood (moved to Harrowgate by next market day), Halan Hollett, Eldette Corrett. Thivie bought ribbon and regretted it; Halan laughed at story nobody else found funny.
